meta.note: Editorial structure for the 'four university rankings disagree' story. Spine: 'best university' is a weighting choice, not a fact. Hero = the reweighter (ana_12 / img_01) in edt_06, produced by the reader before the prose names Oxford/MIT/Michigan. Full earned interactive set curated for a visual+computational topic (hero + 6 distinct supporting playgrounds).

core_claim: "Best university" is a weighting choice, not a fact: four global rankings disagree and even the neutral OpenAlex research-output referee crowns a different order, so no table is simply right — each measures a different definition of "best".

edt_01.label: Hook — Four tables, four champions
edt_01.editorial_notes: Reframe hook — lead with the surprise (four different #1s + Peking's 89-place swing), not background. Exact: Caltech/Harvard/Harvard/MIT (+Michigan referee); only 5 of 15 names in all four top-10s; Peking QS 12 vs ARWU 101 = 89; 23.5% / 19.6% exact. sct_bgm (John Field nocturne) is the mandatory top-of-article now-playing BGM card. Opening interactive = the guess-each-table's-#1 quiz (img_04); it may reveal the four PUBLISHED champions but must NOT spoil the reweighter's Oxford/MIT/Michigan.

edt_02.label: How far apart are they?
edt_02.editorial_notes: Correlations 0.599-0.853 exact (most alike ARWU-CWUR 0.853, least CWUR-QS 0.599); QS is the systematic outlier (its three pairings 0.599/0.647/0.735 are the three lowest). Median spread 122 (122.5), mean 158 (157.8); Stanford spread 2, MIT 5. Chart-led, no forced media.

edt_03.label: The swingers — same school, tens of places apart
edt_03.editorial_notes: Use ONLY the band-free set (schools ranked <=200 by all four systems) per ana_caveat_04 — never the raw George Mason 850 tail-band artefacts. Exact: Peking 12/101, Tsinghua 14/101 (~90 apart), Berkeley 4/27, Caltech THE 1 / OpenAlex-works 82, Fudan spread 161. Campus images: Peking (det_media_08), Tsinghua (det_media_07), Berkeley (det_media_09), Caltech (det_media_06). Supporting interactive = guess-Peking's-spread (img_03).

edt_04.label: Why they disagree — the weighting dial
edt_04.editorial_notes: The mechanical cause. Exact: QS reputation survey 50% (40% academic + 10% employer); THE ~33% survey + 30% citations; ARWU 0%; CWUR 0%; OpenAlex 0%. Flag that the QS 2023 edition uses the PRE-2024 legacy weights (Academic Reputation 40%) per ana_caveat_05 — its reputation-heaviness is edition-specific. Supporting interactive = guess-the-reputation-share quiz (img_11).

edt_05.label: The survey and the microscope disagree
edt_05.editorial_notes: QS internal Academic-Reputation vs Citations-per-Faculty correlate only 0.421. Reputation-lifted (QS>>ARWU): HKU 151/21, NUS 101/11, Peking 101/12. Research-lifted (ARWU>>QS): Vanderbilt 53/199, Maryland 43/164. Chart-led.

edt_06.label: So you decide — set the weights yourself
edt_06.editorial_notes: CENTERPIECE SECTION. The hero reweighter (img_01/ana_12) must render and be usable BEFORE the paragraph that names Oxford (87.02) / MIT (96.25) / Michigan (100.0). The reader produces the '#1 flips' answer themselves. It MUST recompute on the Analyst's audited client_model reweightRankings (code/client_model.js) so the live #1 and the prose figures are two readouts of one model — never a divergent second model. Exact preset #1s: balanced Oxford 87.02, qs_like MIT 96.25, the_like MIT 95.16, arwu_like Michigan 95.24, output_only Michigan 100.0; 3 distinct #1s.

edt_07.label: The neutral referee doesn't settle it either
edt_07.editorial_notes: Exact: OpenAlex #1 by works=Michigan, by cited_by=Harvard, by h_index=Washington; Michigan works #1 but best commercial rank only #17. ARWU tracks OpenAlex most (0.876 vs h_index), QS least (0.636); even the best fit 0.88 is far from 1.0 — the referee vindicates no single table. Campus images: Michigan (det_media_10), Toronto (sct_toronto), UCL (sct_ucl), Washington (sct_washington). Supporting interactive = toggle-the-referee's-lens (img_07). Note the Washington h_index rank is inflated by the two_yr_mean_citedness anomaly (ana_caveat_03) — per-paper impact uses cites/work instead.

edt_08.label: The size trap — papers or impact?
edt_08.editorial_notes: Exact: Michigan works ~980,174 (volume #1) -> cites/work 67.2 (impact #332), a +331-place flip; Caltech volume #82 / impact #13; Princeton #104 / #24; MIT #35 / #3; Harvard #2 / #1. Supporting interactive = guess-Michigan's-impact-rank (img_05).

edt_09.label: Why believe this — the disagreement survives holding the year fixed
edt_09.editorial_notes: VALIDATION BEAT (its own passage) + the MANDATORY era-mismatch sentence, tagged [ana_11, det_14] in prose. Exact: 2015 trio (285 schools) mean Spearman 0.782 (THE-ARWU 0.757, THE-CWUR 0.751, ARWU-CWUR 0.840) — still far below 1.0, so the disagreement is methodological, not a year-mixing artefact. State honestly that QS's 0.660 is an UPPER bound conflated with the ~8-year span; do NOT sell a QS-vs-2015 gap as pure methodology.

edt_10.label: Look up your own university
edt_10.editorial_notes: Reader-as-subject engagement lever. Lookup covers all 218 common-core universities: rank in THE/ARWU/CWUR/QS + OpenAlex (works & cites) + spread. Exact sample spreads: Berkeley 23, Caltech 11, Michigan 8, Peking 89. Supporting interactive = look-up-your-university (img_02, personal_input).

edt_11.label: What "best" actually means
edt_11.editorial_notes: End on tension, not a summary. Controversies as context: QS 2024 cut reputation 40%->30% (schools moved without changing, det_10); Columbia fell 2->18 for false data (det_11); the 2023 Yale/Harvard-led boycott (det_12). Do NOT overclaim rankings are worthless — the point is 'best' is a question the reader must finish. Close on the reweighter: the only honest #1 is the one whose weighting you would defend.

edt_12.label: About the data
edt_12.editorial_notes: Methods appendix (after the close; not the emotional ending). Provenance: 4 commercial systems + OpenAlex (fetched 24 Jun 2026); cleanest cross-system year 2015, QS 2023 + OpenAlex as overlays. The 218-school common core is a normalised-name join and is matcher-dependent (dataset states ~189) — treat ~200 as the scale, not a precise constant (ana_caveat_02). The fine data-quality quirks (ana_01b) live here / in the verify layer, not in body prose.

hero.why_hero: The single contestable headline the reader must produce: dragging the five pillar weights re-ranks all 218 universities live and manufactures Oxford, MIT, or Michigan as world #1 from the same data — proving 'best' is a slider position, not a fact. Recomputes on the Analyst's audited reweightRankings client_model.

supporting.earns_place: Distinct finding: the reader guesses each table's PUBLISHED #1 and discovers four different champions (Caltech/Harvard/MIT + the Michigan referee) exist BEFORE any reweighting. Not a duplicate of the hero (which is the reader manufacturing a champion) — this is 'the tables already disagree as printed'.

Distinct finding: toggling the neutral referee between works / cited_by / h_index crowns Michigan -> Harvard -> Washington — the 'objective' referee opens a new argument instead of settling it. Only playground bound to OpenAlex's own three-way self-disagreement.

Distinct finding: guess where the raw-output #1 (Michigan) lands per-paper, then feel the +331-place plunge (works #1 -> impact #332). Isolates the single normalisation choice (volume vs per-paper) — a different lever than weighting across systems (hero) or across tables (others).

Distinct finding: commit a guess for a famous swinger's per-system ranks, then feel the real 89-place QS-vs-ARWU gap for Peking land data-bound. Makes the single-school swing hands-on — distinct from the aggregate correlation/spread and from the #1-champion findings.

Distinct finding: guess the reputation-survey share of QS, then see QS is 50% surveyed opinion while ARWU and CWUR are 0% — the mechanical CAUSE of the disagreement. No other playground makes the weighting-of-opinion figure producible.

Distinct finding: the reader types their own university (any of 218) and pulls its five verdicts + spread — the reader-as-subject lever. Distinct data (RANK_LOOKUP, per-university vectors) and a distinct 'find yourself in the data' job no other playground covers.
